battle.name: 建州之戰
battle.brief: 建炎四年，私鹽販范汝為於福建建州聚眾十餘萬起事，光澤、順昌饑民響應；官軍一萬人戰於邵武大敗，遂命韓世忠率三萬眾入閩，圍城數月，終以內應夜開城門破之，范汝為退入回源洞自焚。攻城時宋軍列雲梯、撞車、飛石，並列神臂弓於城下，絞弦而發，一發穿重甲，專壓城頭。

kit.name: 神臂弓
kit.history: 以絞弦張臂的強弩，一發穿重甲。宋的邊軍靠它守住了自己的邊界。

countries: 交戰的兩方，一方是南宋朝廷在福建路的官軍與各州縣守軍，一方是建州私鹽販范汝為聚起來的起義眾。福建路在江南東路最西，控扼閩北山區，州縣自南平向北有邵武、光澤、順昌一路，鄰近江西虔州，是兩浙往西南轉運的孔道。南宋在這一帶的常備兵不多，禁軍與廂兵多集中於兩浙、江淮，福建所倚賴的是各縣的巡檢、寨兵與鄉兵弓箭手，裝備自備、常年缺額，一旦有事只能臨時召集；南路主官由福建路安撫司兼兵馬都統統轄，事急則調江西、兩浙之兵入閩，以江西兵為主力。范汝為一方則沒有官府與正式編制，靠的是私鹽販的網路把鹽丁、漁民、失業船戶與饑民串連起來，名義上以范汝為首，眾推其為首領，各處響應者另設頭目分屯。起義席捲建州、邵武、光澤、順昌、浦城一帶，曾攻破州治與縣城，逼得官軍一敗再敗。雙方在兵制上極不對稱：一方有名冊、有糧餉、有攻城器械，另一方有的是人望與熟悉山道的地理。
countriesEn: There were two sides. On one, the officials and garrisons of the Southern Song in Fujian circuit; on the other, the rising mustered at Jianzhou by Fan Ruwei, a salt smuggler. Fujian circuit lay at the far west of the Jiangnan East circuit, commanding the mountains of northern Min, its prefectures and counties running from Nanping northward through Shaowu, Guangze and Shunchang, close to Qian prefecture in Jiangxi, and forming the turning point of the supply road from the Two Zhe toward the south-west. The Song kept few regulars here: the imperial guard and the provincial battalions were concentrated in the Two Zhe and along the Huai and the Yangzi, and what Fujian relied on was the patrol detachments, the garrison companies and the local militia archers of each county, who equipped themselves and were chronically short in numbers, so that in an emergency they could only be mustered on the spot. The southern army was commanded by the pacification commissioner of Fujian together with the regional military commander, and when the emergency came troops were brought in from Jiangxi and the Two Zhe, with Jiangxi soldiers forming the greater part. Fan's side had neither government nor formal organisation: what held it together was the smuggling network of the salt trade, which drew together salt workers, fishermen, boatmen out of work and famine refugees, and it was on the strength of that network that the multitude rallied under Fan as its acknowledged leader, local heads of bands being set over the districts that answered him. The rising swept across Jianzhou, Shaowu, Guangze, Shunchang and Pucheng, took prefectural and county seats, and wore the government troops out again and again. The imbalance in military organisation was extreme: on one side a roster of names, pay, rations and siege engines; on the other, popular support and an intimate knowledge of the mountain tracks.
people: 起義首領范汝為出身私鹽販，早年往來閩浙之間販鹽，聚起了錢糧與人望，饑民附之者眾。起事之後，他自居首領，據建州城以為根本，諸縣皆有頭目聽其號令；但他並非將才，史料所記多是他招募、煽動與周旋官軍招撫之事，真正作戰多由其部將與客軍的頭目指揮。官軍方面，先是江南西路兵馬都統辛企宗，紹興元年秋率兵一萬入閩，十月戰於邵武，為義軍所敗，士卒死傷甚眾，詔落其職。接掌全局的是韓世忠。南渡之初，他以平定苗劉之變與在江淮一線的接戰知名，膽大而詭譎，人稱韓五；他接旨後不急著強攻，先遣人入城探明虛實，又使人偽作販馬商旅、攜貨入城，與城中內應約期開門。城破之日，他自將精騎馳入城門，呼曰城已破，願降者悉免死，於是附義軍者大半潰散；范汝為走保回源洞，火攻不下，遂引火自焚。朝廷方面，紹興元年入為尚書右僕射的秦檧在朝中主政，此役的處置權全在韓世忠一身；而辛企宗因敗被貶，則是官軍在福建接戰失利留下的第一筆帳。
peopleEn: The leader of the rising, Fan Ruwei, was a salt smuggler who had traded salt between Min and Zhe for years, and had gathered money, provisions and a following; many famine refugees attached themselves to him. Once the revolt was under way he took the title of chief, made Jianzhou city his base, and every district had a head of band who took orders from him. He was not a soldier, however: what the records show of him is recruiting, incitement and the business of parrying the court's offers of amnesty, while the fighting was actually led by his own commanders and by the heads of the hired bands. On the government side the first was Xin Qizong, military commander of the Jiangxi West circuit, who led ten thousand men into Fujian in the autumn of the first year of Shaoxing and was beaten at Shaowu in the tenth month, the dead and wounded among his soldiers being heavy, and was stripped of his command by edict. The man who took over the whole affair was Han Shizhong. From the early days of the southern crossing he was known for putting down the Miao-Liu mutiny and for his fighting along the river front, bold and full of ruses, and the people called him Han the Fifth. Given his commission he did not hurry into a direct assault: he first sent men into the city to learn the state of the defence, then had men disguised as horse-dealing merchants enter the town with goods, and arranged with contacts inside for the gate to be opened on a fixed day. On the day the city fell he rode in at the head of his best horse, crying that the city was taken and that all who surrendered would be spared, and thereupon the greater part of those who had joined the rising scattered. Fan Ruwei fell back on Huiyuan Cave, where fire could not be driven in, and so set fire to himself. At court Qin Hui had entered the chancellorship as right vice chancellor in the first year of Shaoxing, but the handling of the affair lay entirely in Han Shizhong's hands; and Xin Qizong's demotion after his defeat was the first entry on the government side's account of failure in Fujian.
kits: 卡面這件神臂弓，是宋代弩兵手中最重的遠射兵器。《武經總要》載其形制：弓身長一尺二寸，矢長二尺五寸，箭闊一寸五分；上弦不用手拉，須以絞弦機關蹶張，上滿一弦往往要數人合力，甚至借馬力，張好之後所發的箭又重又遠，一步之間可以穿重甲，威力遠勝尋常弓弩。宋人索性以神臂名之，與床子弩同列為禁軍與邊鎮守軍的配備重器。在建州之戰裡，神臂弓的位置有兩層：其一在攻城序列中，宋軍把它列在城外營壘後的高地，絞好弦待命，專打城頭守卒與女牆射孔；義軍的守禦多靠木柵、柴垛與薄甲，重弩一發穿甲，射界便被壓住，雲梯上的攀登之卒才有路可上。其二在野戰中，辛企宗一萬人與邵武接戰，宋軍列弩齊射，義軍湧上的步騎一旦被重弩貫穿，陣形即散。與神臂弓並列的攻城器有雲梯、撞竿、飛石砲（宋人以木為架、投石毀城堞與城樓）、火箭與火藥箭，外加壕壘、柴薪與雲梯鹿角；義軍一方則以雜兵當之，鹽刀、漁叉、標槍、竹籤、柴草、拒馬，數量雖多而器械陳舊。糧秣方面，官軍自江西運糧、順閩江而下，水陸轉輸才是這一戰真正的難處。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card face, the shenbi crossbow, was the heaviest long-range weapon in the hands of Song crossbowmen. The Wujing Zongyao describes its form: the bow was one foot two inches long, the arrow two feet five inches, and the shaft of the arrow an inch and a half wide; the string was not drawn by hand but had to be cocked with a windlass mechanism, so that cocking a single string often took several men working together, sometimes with the help of a horse, and once cocked the arrow that flew was both heavy and long-ranging, able to pass through heavy armour at a single step's distance, far surpassing the power of an ordinary bow or crossbow. The Song named it after the divine strength it took to draw, and ranked it with the bed-nu crossbow as a heavy weapon in the issue of the imperial guard and of the frontier garrisons. In the war at Jianzhou the crossbow had two places. First in the siege sequence: the Song put it behind the camp on rising ground outside the walls, cocked and ready, to shoot the defenders on the parapet and the embrasures; the rebels relied on wooden barriers, stacked brushwood and thin armour, and once a heavy bolt went through a cuirass the firing line was suppressed, so that the men on the scaling ladders had a path to climb. Second in the open field: at Shaowu, against Xin Qizong's ten thousand, the Song fired its crossbows in line, and once the rebel foot and horse pressing forward were run through by the heavy bolts, their formation came apart. Alongside the shenbi crossbow in the siege train stood scaling ladders, battering poles, stone-throwers (Song catapults built on wooden frames, hurling stones to break parapets and towers), fire arrows and gunpowder arrows, together with trenches, brushwood and mantlets; the rebels answered with miscellaneous weapons, salt knives, fishing forks, javelins, bamboo stakes, brushwood and caltrops, numerous but obsolete. As for supply, the grain for the Song army came down from Jiangxi along the Min river, and the slow business of moving it by land and water was the true difficulty of the campaign.
tactics: 官軍的攻城有一條清楚的次第。先是斷糧斷水：建州城倚山而建，松溪自城中流過，官軍沿溪設柵、壅上流，把城內的水路與山道封死；再在城外築營壘，挖壕、築壘牆，把城四面圍住，逼義軍不能出城覓食，久之自潰。第三步是造器械、削射界：以飛石砲擊打城堞與城樓，以火箭射城上的柴草棚屋，並把神臂弓架在營壘後面，絞好弦待命，雲梯一靠城，弩手便齊射城頭，把守卒壓得抬不起身。第四步最要緊，是內應：韓世忠先遣人反覆偵察城中守備與人心，認定城門守備與守軍將領之間有隙可乘，才使人偽作販馬商旅、攜貨入城，與內應約定日期，屆時以火為號開門；大軍再以撞竿撞開門扇，雲梯同時靠城，攻守之勢一瞬間倒轉。城破之後沒有巷戰的僵持：范汝為率殘部退入回源洞，官軍火攻，洞中無水，人馬俱焚，餘眾或降或散，逃入山區者後來成了新的盜源。義軍的防禦則是死守：以柴草塞門道，門上覆濕泥、置滾木，城市街巷設拒馬與陷坑，城頭以標槍、石塊、弓弩拒敵；義軍士卒多無重甲，只能靠人多與地勢硬撐。
tacticsEn: The government assault followed a clear order of business. First to cut off food and water: Jianzhou was built against the hill and the Song stream ran through the town, so the troops set up barriers along the stream and dammed it above, sealing the water road and the mountain paths that led out; then they built camps outside the city, dug trenches and raised breastworks, enclosing the town on all sides so that the rebels could not go out to forage, and trust that famine would do the rest. The third step was to build engines and cut the firing line: stone-throwers broke the parapets and towers, fire arrows set the brushwood sheds on the walls alight, and behind the camp the shenbi crossbows were cocked and stood ready, so that when the ladders touched the wall the crossbowmen fired in volleys at the parapet and held the defenders down. The fourth step was the most delicate, and it was the one that won the day. Han Shizhong sent men in and out again and again to learn the state of the defence and the mood of the town, and only when he judged that the gate guard and the officer in command were at odds with one another did he have men disguised as horse merchants go in with their goods, and come to an arrangement with contacts inside for the gate to be opened on a set day, a fire being the signal; the main force then drove a battering pole against the gate leaves while the ladders came up at the same moment, and the balance of the assault and the defence was reversed in an instant. Once the wall was broken there was no drawn-out struggle in the streets. Fan Ruwei led what was left back into Huiyuan Cave, the troops set fire to it, there being no water inside, and men and horses were burned together; the rest either surrendered or scattered, and those who got away into the mountains became a new source of bandits. The rebel defence was simply to hold: brushwood packed into the gateways, the doors covered with wet clay and rollers set above them, caltrops and pits dug across the streets of the city, javelins, stones and bows on the parapet. The rebel soldiers for the most part had no heavy armour and could only hold on by numbers and by the advantage of the ground.
data: 史籍留下的數字不多，而且多帶誇張，只能當量級看。起義眾的規模，《宋史》等書記載作十餘萬，諸說並存，或作數萬，實際能列陣作戰的應遠少於此；同一批記載又把起義的時間壓縮在數月之內，說明史家對這場戰事所知有限。官軍方面有明確的數字：辛企宗入閩之兵約一萬；韓世忠奉命率眾三萬入閩，其中當有禁軍、江西與兩浙調來的兵，也有隨軍工匠與運糧的民夫。圍城的時間，諸說多作數月，記攻之三月而克者有，記自十月至春者也有，具體月日仍存爭議。距離上，邵武至建州約二百里，建州至福州五百餘里，建州至江西虔州近千里，糧食與援兵主要走閩江與陸路，冬季閩北山道泥濘，運轉遲緩。把這幾個數字放在一起，可以看出這一戰的真正瓶頸不在打法，而在糧與路。
dataEn: The figures that survive in the records are few, and several are plainly inflated, so they can only be read as orders of magnitude. The size of the rising is given in the Song History and elsewhere as more than a hundred thousand, though other accounts say only several tens of thousands and the men who could actually be drawn up in battle must have been far fewer; the same compilation also squeezes the whole rising into a space of a few months, which shows how little the historians really knew of this war. The government side has firmer numbers: Xin Qizong brought about ten thousand men into Fujian; Han Shizhong was ordered in with a force of thirty thousand, which must have included imperial guard, troops drawn from Jiangxi and the Two Zhe, and the craftsmen and porters who travelled with the army to move its grain. As for the duration of the siege, most accounts make it a matter of months: some say the city was taken in three months, others that the business ran from the tenth month through to the spring, and the exact months and days remain in dispute. In distance, Shaowu lies some two hundred li from Jianzhou, Jianzhou some five hundred and more li from Fuzhou and close to a thousand li from Qian prefecture in Jiangxi; grain and reinforcements came chiefly by the Min river and by road, and the mountain tracks of northern Min were mud in winter, so the movement was slow. Set these figures side by side and the real bottleneck of this campaign becomes plain: it lay not in method but in grain and road.
cause: 起義的根由有三層。最深的一層是鹽。南渡之後兩淮鹽場盡失，國用仰賴東南，朝廷便在兩浙、福建沿海加緊緝私，鹽價抬高，私鹽販的生意越做越大，沿海的鹽丁、漁民、船戶生計逼到絕路，聚集在范汝為這樣一個有錢又有門路的人周圍。第二層是戰後的秩序崩壞。建炎三年金兵南下，直抵杭州、在建康一線反覆掃掠，江南東路各處的廂兵、鄉兵或散或逃，縣裡的武備只剩空架子；而福建遠在千里之外，朝廷一時調不動兵，只能靠地方自己守。第三層是人禍與天災。建炎四年前後浙東、浙西連年水旱，饑民流亡到閩北，光澤、順昌一帶聚了無數饑民；官府倉廩空虛，賑濟不力，饑民既成群，又拿著弓刀，在這個情形下，一句號召、一個能帶頭的人，就足以把饑民變成軍隊。私鹽的網、饑民的隊伍、朝廷的無兵，三件事疊在一起，成了建炎四年福建這場戰爭的全部起因。
causeEn: There were three layers behind the rising. The deepest was salt. After the crossing of the river the salt works of the Two Huai were lost for good, the state's revenue came to depend on the south-east, and the court tightened the suppression of smuggling along the coasts of the Two Zhe and Fujian; the price of salt rose, the trade in smuggled salt grew, and the salt workers, fishermen and boatmen of the coast were driven to the edge of subsistence, gathering around a man with money and connections like Fan Ruwei. The second layer was the collapse of order after the war. In the third year of Jianyan the Jurchen armies drove south as far as Hangzhou, scouring the region around Jiankang again and again; the provincial battalions and local militia of the Jiangnan East circuit scattered or fled, and the armament of the counties was little more than an empty shell, while Fujian lay a thousand li away and the court could not move troops there in time, so the defence of the region had to be left to the locals. The third layer was misfortune and famine. Around the fourth year of Jianyan the Two Zhe suffered years of flood and drought in turn, and famine refugees moved into northern Min, where enormous numbers of them gathered at Guangze and Shunchang; the granaries were empty and relief was not organised, and the refugees were already massed together and already had bows and knives in their hands. Under those conditions a single call and a single man willing to lead at the front were enough to turn a crowd of hungry people into an army. The smuggling network, the band of famine refugees and the absence of troops from the court, laid one upon another, made up the whole origin of the war in Fujian in the fourth year of Jianyan.
impact: 這一場平叛的直接後果，是福建重新回到朝廷手裡：建州城收復，府縣的印信歸位，秩序表面上恢復了。但代價與遺留的問題都不小。義軍散入閩北山區之後，餘眾化為流寇，靠劫掠、劫鹽為生；與此同時官軍在剿辦過程中反覆用兵，民間的田產與戶口受了重創，到紹興末年閩中仍未完全安定，地方志書中建炎、紹興間的饑荒與盜賊記載，往往就指這一段。鹽法這邊，朝廷的反應是加緊緝私、加派鹽額，福建沿海的私販網路被打得更碎，民間的怨氣卻沒有散去，壓力反而更重；這是南渡之後東南社會矛盾的一個縮影，也是後來沿海抗金力量與地方亂事之間那種複雜關係的開端。軍制方面，此役之後朝廷更看重江南各路的守城能力，弓弩、尤其是可穿重甲的神臂弓，成為沿江沿邊城鎮的常備重器，射界、弩數與守城器械的配額漸漸有了定制；幾十年後的采石之役，宋軍以神臂弓壓金人騎兵，用的正是這一路家數。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the suppression was that Fujian came back into the court's hands: Jianzhou was retaken, the seals of the prefectures and counties were restored, and on the surface order returned. But the costs and the residue of the problem were both considerable. After the rebels scattered into the mountains of northern Min, the remnant turned into brigands living on plunder and on seized salt; at the same time the government armies went on campaigning through the region, and the fields and households of the people were badly damaged, so that northern Fujian was not fully settled even by the end of the Shaoxing reign, and the entries for famine and banditry in the local gazetteers for the Jianyan and Shaoxing years generally refer to these years. On salt, the court's answer was to tighten the suppression of smuggling and to increase the salt quotas; the smuggling network along the Fujian coast was broken into smaller pieces, but the resentment of the people did not disperse, and the pressure grew heavier instead. This was a miniature of the social contradictions of the south-east after the crossing of the river, and the opening of the complicated relation that would later hold between the coastal forces resisting the Jin and the local disturbances. In military organisation, the court after this campaign valued the capacity of the Jiangnan circuits to hold walled towns all the more, and bows and crossbows, above all the shenbi crossbow that could pierce heavy armour, became standard heavy equipment in the garrison towns of the river and the frontier, with the firing positions, the number of crossbows and the issue of siege engines gradually fixed by regulation; and decades later, in the battle of Caishi, the Song pressed the Jin cavalry with shenbi crossbows, following exactly this line of armament.
result: 結果是官軍得手。紹興元年冬韓世忠三萬眾入閩，圍建州數月，以內應夜開城門、雲梯同時靠城而破之；范汝為退保回源洞，火攻不退，遂引火自焚，部眾潰散：附者給糧遣散歸農，逃者入山為盜，數年之後才由後續的討捕逐步削平。城雖克，役並非全勝：辛企宗一萬人在邵武覆沒是前車之鑑，圍城數月之間官軍也有因水土、瘴癘與糧運而致的病亡與逃亡。韓世忠本人此役之後並不得志，他以破賊之功召回內地，隨即轉入江淮、楚州一線，與朝中主和的取向頗多不合，功賞與冷落相伴而至。從全局看，這一場戰爭結束了范汝為的十餘萬眾，卻沒有解決引出這十餘萬眾的那些事：鹽仍然要吃，饑仍然要餓，朝廷的兵仍然遠在千里之外。閩北的表面平靜之下，舊的問題原封不動地留了下來。
resultEn: In the end the government troops had their way. In the winter of the first year of Shaoxing Han Shizhong entered Fujian with thirty thousand men, surrounded Jianzhou for a number of months and took the city when the gate was opened from within at night and the ladders came up at the same moment. Fan Ruwei fell back on Huiyuan Cave, fire could not be driven in, and he set fire to himself; his followers scattered, those who surrendered being given grain and sent back to the fields, while those who escaped turned bandits in the mountains and were only worn down gradually by the campaigns that followed over the next several years. The city was taken, but the campaign was not a clean win. The destruction of Xin Qizong's ten thousand at Shaowu was the warning, and during the months of the siege the government army suffered sickness, deaths and desertion from the climate, the miasma and the grain runs. Han Shizhong himself gained little from it: recalled to the interior on the credit of his success against the rebels, he was moved at once to the line of the Yangzi and Chu prefecture, out of step with the court's preference for peace, and reward and cold neglect came to him together. Seen whole, this war ended the hundred thousand of Fan's followers without resolving any of the things that had produced them. Salt still had to be eaten, hunger still had to be fed, and the court's soldiers were still a thousand li away. Beneath the outward calm of northern Min the old problems were left standing exactly where they had been.
